sentences.text: For the Petitioner(s) : Mr. M. A. Sheikh, Advocate For the Respondent(s) : Ms. P. R. Mahanta, SC, Revenue  : Mr. D. Gogoi, Standing Counsel  : Mr. H. Sharma, Government Advocate  : Ms. K. Phukan, CGC

BEFORE  HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE DEVASHIS BARUAH  ORDER Date : 12.08.2024 Heard Mr. M. A. Sheikh, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Petitioners and Ms. K. Phukan, the learned C.G.C. appearing on behalf of the Respondent No.1.

I have also heard P. R. Mahanta, the learned Standing counsel appearing on behalf of the Revenue and Disaster Management Department; Mr. D. Gogoi, the learned Standing counsel appearing on behalf of the Respondent Nos. 2, 4 and 5; Mr. H. Sharma, the learned Government Advocate appears on behalf of the Respondent Nos. 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10.

2. Seventy-three writ Petitioners have joined together and filed the instant writ petition seeking a direction upon the Respondents to return the Schedule-B land to the Petitioners or in the alternative to acquire the land and pay compensation in terms with Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, Page No.# 17/19 2013 (for short "the Act of 2013").

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In addition to that, the Petitioners have also prayed that the Respondent Authorities may be directed to allow the petitioners to harvest the jute cultivation standing on the Schedule-B land for the interest of justice.

It is relevant to take note of that the Schedule-B land is a plot of land measuring 3000 Bighas situated at Revenue Villages : Tengaguri Non-K (Hamurchar),
Kourihagi (Chube Char), Kisanguri (Kasem Char), Kashiguri (Kashem Char), Tenguri (Hamurchar)
Page No.# 1/19 vs The Union Of India And 9 Ors on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123989117/
15 under Laharighat Revenue Circle in the District of Morigaon (erstwhile Nagaon District).
3.

It is apposite herein to mention that prior to filing the instant writ petition, the petitioners have joined together and filed another writ petition which was registered and numbered as WP(C)
No.4916/2023.

The relief sought for in the instant writ petition is the same with WP(C)
No.4916/2023.

In the said writ petition, when the matter was taken up by the Coordinate Bench of this Court, it was submitted that the petitioners be permitted to harvest the jute which the petitioners have cultivated in the land which have been specifically described in Schedule- B land.

However, taking into account that the petitioners had not approached the concerned Respondent Authorities, this Court had given the liberty to the Petitioners to approach the concerned Respondent Authorities.
Under such circumstances, the said writ petition was withdrawn without any liberty.
4. Pursuant thereto, a representation was submitted to the Respondent Nos. 6, 7 and 8 on 31.08.2023.
A perusal of the said representation shows that the petitioners herein claimed that they should be permitted to harvest the said jute which is valued at Rs.1.5 crores.
Thereupon, as Page No.# 18/19 the petitioners have not received any favourable response, the instant writ petition has been filed.
5. This Court has duly heard the learned counsel for the petitioners as well as the counsels who represent the respondents.

6. Pursuant to the order dated 30.07.2024, Mr. D. Gogoi, the learned Standing counsel for the Forest Department has placed various documents which would show that in pursuance to the provisions under Section 35 of the Wild Life (Protection) Act 1972, 200.32 sq. Kms. of area have been notified as the 2nd addition to Orang National Park.

The learned Standing counsel for the Forest Department further drawing the attention of this Court to the various notifications and corrigendum submitted that the Orang National Park is situated in the Districts of Darrang and Sonitpur and not in Morigaon.
In addition to that, he therefore submitted that as per the 2nd addition of the Orang National Park, no land of the petitioners have been brought within the scope of the said notification.

The learned Standing counsel further submitted that notifications were issued calling for objections and there was no objections also being filed by any person and it is under such circumstances, the Speaking Order has also been passed on 22.07.2022.

The documents which have been placed before this Court are collectively kept on record and marked with the letter "X".
7.

In the backdrop of the above, if this Court duly takes note of the case of the petitioners, it would be seen that the petitioners claims that they are the owners of the land which have been specifically described in Schedule-B to the wit petition.
The question arises as to whether this Court in exercise of the powers under Article 226 of the Constitution can Page No.# 19/19 at all adjudicate the said aspect of the matter.
In the opinion of this Court, such adjudication would require detailed evidence being tendered, records being perused which can only be done by a competent Court of civil jurisdiction.
In addition to that, the claim of all the petitioners are individual claims as regards their right, title and interest.

Such claims cannot be decided collectively in a proceeding under Article 226 Page No.# 1/19 vs The Union Of India And 9 Ors on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123989117/
16 of the Constitution that too when the Respondents do not admit that the lands of the Petitioners were taken.

entities.text: 1/19 vs The Union Of India And 9
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, this Court is not inclined to entertain the instant writ petition for which the instant writ petition stands dismissed.

8. It is however observed that the petitioners herein are always be at liberty to approach the competent Civil Court seeking their right, title and interest over the land as well as for recovery of possession or other relief(s) as deem fit.
The dismissal of the instant writ petition shall not prejudice the Petitioners in any proceedings initiated before the Civil Court.

Seventy-three writ Petitioners have joined together and filed the instant writ petition seeking a direction upon the Respondents to return the Schedule-B land to the Petitioners or in the alternative to acquire the land and pay compensation in terms with Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, Page No.# 17/19 2013 (for short "the Act of 2013").
In the said writ petition, when the matter was taken up by the Coordinate Bench of this Court, it was submitted that the petitioners be permitted to harvest the jute which the petitioners have cultivated in the land which have been specifically described in Schedule- B land.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The learned Standing counsel for the Forest Department further drawing the attention of this Court to the various notifications and corrigendum submitted that the Orang National Park is situated in the Districts of Darrang and Sonitpur and not in Morigaon.
In addition to that, he therefore submitted that as per the 2nd addition of the Orang National Park, no land of the petitioners have been brought within the scope of the said notification.
The learned Standing counsel further submitted that notifications were issued calling for objections and there was no objections also being filed by any person and it is under such circumstances, the Speaking Order has also been passed on 22.07.2022.

In the backdrop of the above, if this Court duly takes note of the case of the petitioners, it would be seen that the petitioners claims that they are the owners of the land which have been specifically described in Schedule-B to the wit petition.
In the opinion of this Court, such adjudication would require detailed evidence being tendered, records being perused which can only be done by a competent Court of civil jurisdiction.
In addition to that, the claim of all the petitioners are individual claims as regards their right, title and interest.
Such claims cannot be decided collectively in a proceeding under Article 226 Page No.# 1/19 vs The Union Of India And 9 Ors on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123989117/
16 of the Constitution that too when the Respondents do not admit that the lands of the Petitioners were taken.
